briefing.text: Indirect evidence is not a substitute for a paired panel-vs-WES comparison. Showing that panel TMB predicts an outcome (progression-free survival, durable clinical benefit, independence from PD-L1) the way WES TMB does in other cohorts, or that panel TMB tracks another panel-derived feature such as fraction of genome altered (FGA), says nothing about the sample-level correlation between panel and WES estimates; paired studies have found that panel and WES TMB can differ in outcome prediction on the very same specimens. Before any modelling, list which columns could serve as the WES measurement. If there are none, confirm for each candidate proxy (MUTATION_RATE, TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS, mutation counts, FGA) whether it derives from the targeted assay. If only such proxies exist, do not report outcome associations or panel-internal correlations as support for, or contradiction of, a claim about panel-vs-WES correlation.
briefing.reason: The clinical tables invite outcome or FGA analyses of panel TMB; without this the team could present such an association as an answer to a question it cannot address, which would change the label.

briefing.text: Evidence standard for a 'do not correlate' claim. A non-significant p-value alone does not support it (absence of evidence), and it is contradicted only by a paired analysis that shows a positive correlation; showing lack of association needs an equivalence-style argument and often a large n. First confirm for yourself whether paired panel and WES TMB values exist on the same tumours. If they do, report the correlation with a 95 percent confidence interval and read it three ways: interval wholly above zero contradicts the claim; interval wholly inside a small band around zero (for example |r| < 0.3) supports it; an interval that straddles both is inconclusive. If no paired values exist at all, neither support nor contradiction can be computed from these tables: do not fill the gap with general knowledge about how panel TMB usually relates to WES TMB, and choose the label from what the tables can test, using the task's own label definitions.
briefing.reason: It fixes in advance what result counts as support, contradiction or neither, and stops the team from answering from background knowledge instead of from the data; either mistake would flip the label.

briefing.text: Two sample-level factors can weaken a TMB comparison for reasons that are not the targeted assay's fault; they matter only if a paired panel-vs-WES analysis turns out to be possible. (a) Tumour purity and depth: panels are sequenced to several hundred x and WES to about 100 to 200x, so in low-purity tumours (below about 30 percent) WES misses low-allele-fraction clonal variants and underestimates TMB while the panel does not. A weak pooled correlation can therefore come from the low-purity subgroup. Check: use each sample's median variant allele fraction, t_alt_count/(t_ref_count+t_alt_count) from data_mutations.txt, as a purity proxy and compare the correlation in the high- and low-VAF halves; if they differ, report the stratified correlations and do not attribute the low-purity discordance to the panel. (b) Matched normal: tumour-only (unmatched) calling leaves germline variants in the mutation list and inflates TMB, most of all on small panels. Check: tabulate SOMATIC_STATUS in data_clinical_sample.txt (Matched vs Unmatched), see whether Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode and n_ref_count/n_alt_count are filled in data_mutations.txt, and compare TMB distributions between matched and unmatched samples. If unmatched samples are present, make matched samples the primary analysis, show unmatched ones as a sensitivity analysis, and do not read an inflated unmatched TMB as assay disagreement.
briefing.reason: If paired values exist, a low pooled correlation could be wrongly taken as support for the hypothesis when it is produced by low-purity or unmatched samples; these checks change which samples go into the primary analysis and how a weak result is read.

shared_assumptions: Both teams read the hypothesis as requiring a paired, same-tumour comparison of two independently sequenced TMB values, and treated the absence of a WES column as the absence of any 'relevant variable'. Neither tested whether any other construction inside the tables (for example a comparison that is not part-whole) could count as relevant, or argued explicitly why it could not.

Both teams decided the platform of every sample from labels (GENE_PANEL, gene panel matrix, sample-ID suffix, Score='MSK-IMPACT') and from gene breadth (385 genes). Neither used a label-independent fingerprint of the assay, such as per-sample tumour and normal read depth from t_ref_count/t_alt_count/n_ref_count.

Both teams assumed the samples where MUTATION_RATE is not reproduced from the mutation file (about 9 to 13 percent of samples) are harmless curation differences within one panel call set. Neither checked whether those samples form a structured subgroup.

Both teams assumed the label definition for 'Not verifiable' applies when one of the two quantities in the claim (panel TMB) is present and the other (WES TMB) is absent. This is a reading of the task rule, not something either team tested.
unused_evidence: Patient table column IRB (Commercial 186, Clinical trial 54): a cohort split that neither team crossed with the TMB-column mismatches or with any provenance field. A second assay, if any existed, would most plausibly sit in a sub-cohort.
Read-depth columns in data_mutations.txt (t_ref_count, t_alt_count, n_ref_count, n_alt_count): filled in all rows but used by neither team as evidence of which assay produced each call.

The one sample whose 35 mutation rows carry Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode='NORMAL' (blank in the other 2482 rows), four of them with blank Center, Score and Validation_Status; plus 5 rows with Mutation_Status UNKNOWN. Both teams saw these and kept them without establishing where the rows come from.
The single mutated gene (1 of 385) that lies outside the 517-gene CNA list: neither team named it or said whether it is an alias or an off-panel call.

Sample-ID tumour numbers (T01 212, T02 27, T03 1) show that other specimens of some patients exist outside these files; not usable here but relevant to the claim that no second measurement per patient exists.

PFS_MONTHS, PFS_STATUS, DURABLE_CLINICAL_BENEFIT, PDL1_SCORE, FGA, data_cna.txt, data_cna_hg19.seg and data_sv.txt were set aside on purpose as indirect evidence. I agree that none of them is a WES measurement; data_cna.txt marks the same 43 genes NA in every panel version, so it does not even encode panel-version gene lists.
unresolved_weak_points: Team A: the label rests on a judgement about the task's definitions, not on a statistic. Reported, not resolved.
Team A: did not explain why MUTATION_RATE differs from the mutation file in about 9 percent of samples (implied count off by -4 to +3). Reported, not resolved.
Team B: same definitional weak point (strict reading of the rule; a WES subset may exist outside these files). Reported, not resolved, and not resolvable from the data.

Team B: 32 of 240 samples have MUTATION_RATE off from count/panel Mb and one sample has rows in a different annotation format; both dismissed as 'minor curation' without a check of which samples they are. Team B's pitfalls_checked list is empty.
second_readings: 'Do not correlate with WES' read as a paired, same-tumour correlation (both teams) versus read as a general claim that a panel-sized target cannot estimate the burden of a wider territory, which could be probed inside panel data only by comparing disjoint gene sets. The second reading is weaker and the teams may reasonably reject it, but neither stated why.

'Relevant variables' in the label rule read as 'both quantities named in the claim' (both teams) versus 'any quantity named in the claim'. Panel TMB is present; under the looser reading the data hold a relevant variable but give no evidence in either direction, which the three labels do not cleanly cover.
'Estimates of TMB' could mean per-Mb rates (MUTATION_RATE, TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS) or raw counts; both teams handled this and it does not change anything without a WES value.
challenge.verdict: I trust the agreed answer's factual basis fairly well: my own reading of the file structure confirms one sample per patient, only three targeted-panel versions in every table, a single-centre call set and no exome-scale or second-platform field. The remaining risk is not in the data analysis but in how the label rule is read when one of the two quantities in the claim is present and the other absent, plus three small loose ends (the unexplained MUTATION_RATE mismatches, the one oddly formatted sample, the one off-list gene) that both teams reported without resolving.

findings.question: In cBioPortal-format study files, how are the clinical sample attributes 'Mutation Rate' (MUTATION_RATE) and 'TMB (nonsynonymous)' (TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS) each defined for targeted-panel samples: which variant classes are counted, which denominator is used, and is each value supplied by the study's data curators or computed by the portal from the mutation file?
findings.answer: Partly settled. TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS is not supplied by the study's authors: cBioPortal's datahub curators add it with their own TMB script (datahub-study-curation-tools/tmb), computed from the study's MAF. It was added to all 71 targeted-panel studies in August 2021 (datahub PR 1463) after a coding-sequence (CDS) length was added to each of 52 gene panels; the curation guide says the TMB column 'should be added, generated by this script'. It counts nonsynonymous variants only (cBioPortal's lead confirms silent variants are excluded; exome studies divide the nonsynonymous count by 30 Mb). For panel studies the denominator is the gene panel's CDS length: that is the stated purpose of the CDS field, but I could not open the script's README, so the exact Variant_Classification list and any minimum panel size are unconfirmed. Non-protein-coding panel genes are excluded from the calculation. MUTATION_RATE is not defined on any cBioPortal page I read. The curation guide names only the TMB column as script-generated, so MUTATION_RATE is by elimination a column delivered by the data provider; its variant classes and denominator are not settled by the web. Implication for the unexplained mismatch: it can arise from definitional differences (variant classes counted, excluded non-coding genes, per-sample panel version, or a MAF revised after the column was computed). No page read says either column draws on a second assay such as exome sequencing, but for MUTATION_RATE that is unproven, not excluded.
findings.confidence: medium (high that TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS is computed by cBioPortal curators from the MAF with nonsynonymous variants only; medium on the panel CDS denominator; low on MUTATION_RATE, which the web did not define)

findings.question: In the methodological literature on validating targeted-panel tumour mutational burden against whole-exome sequencing, which study designs are accepted as evidence about panel-versus-exome correlation: paired sequencing of the same tumours on both assays, in-silico restriction of exome calls to panel genes, or any analysis that uses panel data alone (for example comparing disjoint gene subsets of a panel)? Is any panel-only analysis regarded as informative about panel-versus-exome correlation?
findings.answer: Two designs are accepted, and both need an exome-derived value for the same tumours. (a) In-silico restriction: exome calls (usually TCGA) are restricted to the panel's genes and compared with full-exome TMB. This is the Friends of Cancer Research phase I design (eleven laboratories, TCGA MC3 exomes, panel TMB regressed on exome TMB); the authors describe it as characterising 'theoretical' variability. (b) Empirical paired sequencing of the same tumours on the panel and on exome, which is the stronger design. Exome TMB is the gold or reference standard in both. No source I read treats a panel-only analysis as evidence about panel-versus-exome correlation. Correlating disjoint gene subsets of one panel measures the panel's internal consistency and sampling noise; panel-size modelling gives a model-based precision estimate, not an observed correlation with exome. The teams' shared assumption is therefore consistent with the literature read. Caveats: this rests on a few reviews and consortium papers, not an exhaustive search; the reader returned only the opening sections of the three pages opened this session, so the paired-design statement leans on pages this department read in an earlier session.
findings.confidence: medium (high that in-silico and paired designs are the accepted ones; medium that no panel-only design is accepted, because that is absence of evidence in a limited reading)

findings.question: In MAF-format mutation files exported from a clinical targeted-sequencing pipeline, what does it mean when a small block of rows has a generic Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode value such as 'NORMAL' and blank Center and Score fields while all other rows have the barcode blank and the centre and assay name filled: is this a known sign of rows merged from a different pipeline version or annotation pass, or of a different assay?
findings.answer: Not settled by the web: no page documents this pattern as a marker of a different assay. What is documented: the vcf2maf converter (MSKCC) hard-codes the defaults tumor_id 'TUMOR', normal_id 'NORMAL' and centre '.', so the literal 'NORMAL' is the placeholder written when no normal sample ID is passed to the tool (its README says to omit --normal-id when there was no matched normal). In cBioPortal's MAF format, Center and Matched_Norm_Sample_Barcode are optional free-text columns. My reading: those rows went through a different conversion or annotation path from the rest of the file. That fits rows added or re-annotated separately, but it neither shows nor excludes a second sequencing source, and the placeholder alone is not evidence of exome or another assay. The assay-bearing fields of those rows (Sequencer, Sequence_Source, Validation_Method, read depths, whether the genes lie inside the panel) are what would decide it. Note that vcf2maf's default centre is '.', not blank, so the blank Center and Score are not explained by that default.
findings.confidence: low for the interpretation (high only for the fact that 'NORMAL' is vcf2maf's default placeholder)
